claim: A glowing ghost-light — a soft luminous core wreathed in wispy tendrils that drift and bob, its halo melting into a soft volume like a marsh spirit.

q1_defects.answer: No hard tile-grid or shelf banding. All frames show organic flowing haze with no horizontal grid seams or repeated square cloud cells — the round-1 tiled-grid artifact is gone. bandingScore stays low (0.138-0.167 on play frames; the caveat notes it over-reports on organic haze, and by eye there are no hard seams). No cut-off, no misalignment, backend=webgpu, zero console/network errors.
evidence: metrics: play-2 bandingScore=0.167 (<0.25), idle bandingScore=0.141; consoleErrors=[] networkErrors=[]

q2_reads_as.answer: Reads clearly as a luminous coloured ghost-light, NOT a colorless white blob. Idle and play frames show a bright magenta/pink core wreathed in soft drifting tendrils and haze melting into a soft volume — matching the marsh-spirit claim. effHue holds ~344-347 (magenta/pink), an explicitly acceptable eerie-wisp colour per the caveats, at effSat ~0.27-0.34. Colour survives now; the only near-white region is the very center of the glowSize-HIGH extreme, which is still wreathed in saturated magenta and reads as a bloom, not the round-1 blown-out white blob.
evidence: metrics: idle effHue=347 effSat=0.27 magentaFrac=0.46; play-3 effHue=347 effSat=0.29

q3_discoverable.answer: Yes. The labeled 'wisps' control produces an obvious, sensible change: low (=2) shows two faint dim wisp lights; high (=6) shows many bright distinct wisp lights spread across the frame. The glowSize control also reads correctly: low = small tight pinprick cores, high = a large blooming halo. driftSpeed is a motion-rate control (paused-sweep changed=false is expected per the caveats).
evidence: control: wisps low->high satPixels 1578->3941, magentaFrac 0.38->0.53, changed=true

q4_responsive.answer: Responsive. Visible motion across all three play frames — the core morphs shape, tendrils break off and drift, satellite wisps appear and move. Control apply latency is low and consistent (~580-597ms).
evidence: metrics: play-1 frameDeltaMag=5.78, play-2=3.65, play-3=13.98 (non-zero, visibly different frames)

q5_net.answer: A user would be PLEASED — it now looks like a real glowing marsh-spirit with a coloured luminous core and soft drifting tendrils, the ugly tile-grid is gone, and the wisps slider visibly adds more ghost-lights. All three round-1 blockers are resolved.
evidence: metrics: play frames bandingScore<=0.167, effHue~347 (coloured, not white)

flags.note: At the glowSize-HIGH extreme the core center blooms to near-white; it is still wreathed in saturated magenta so it reads as a luminous bloom rather than a colorless blob, but the brightest extreme of that slider loses some core colour. Taste-level, not a blocker.
driftSpeed sweep frames are near-identical (changed=false) — expected for a motion-rate control captured paused, but the sweep does not self-demonstrate the effect.
flags.evidence: control: driftSpeed low/mid/high effHue=344 effSat~0.33 essentially identical, changed=false
